weakest_line: with the first consequence God named.
one_fix: Repair the broken second line, then anchor each 'what would change' point in a quoted Genesis 2-3 detail instead of speculation like great-grandparents at the dinner table. Cut the channel plug from the close.

weakest_line: Because it was the only thing standing between a family and death.
one_fix: Actually answer the hook from the text: a lamb died in the firstborn's place, and 'the blood shall be to you for a token' (Ex 12:13). Link it to 'Christ our passover' (1 Cor 5:7). Cut the Egypt backstory recap and fix the garbled lines ('At death struck', the missing 'except').

weakest_line: People ask this in our comments all the time.
one_fix: Drop the three-answer lecture and the survey of views. Build the whole script on one case (Cornelius: what he knew, what God did) so there is one clear payoff. End on a real question instead of assuming the viewer had someone tell them about Jesus.

weakest_line: But Judges tells us whose strength it was.
one_fix: Fix the 'every time' overclaim. The Gaza gate verse (Judges 16:3), which is the hook's own example, has no 'Spirit rushed upon him' line, so either address that night directly or say 'again and again.' Also show the pillars collapse after the prison prayer so the prayer pays off on screen.

weakest_line: Historically, Nineveh was one of Assyria's great cities.
one_fix: Give the stakes up front: Assyria was Israel's brutal enemy and would later wipe out the northern kingdom. Then Jonah's 'I knew you are gracious' lands as a real shock instead of a mild surprise.

Cut the colleague and job analogy. Use the time for Judas throwing back the silver and saying 'I have sinned' (Matt 27:3-5) so the contrast with Peter's return is shown, not summarized. Fix the garbled 'While Judas felt remorse, but' line.

weakest_line: But God still using you doesn't mean He approves of how you're living.
one_fix: Open on Samson's puzzle (his strength worked even the night in Gaza), not a sermon question aimed at 'you'. Prove the answer with the text's mechanism (the Spirit of the LORD came upon him for a mission, Judges 13:5) instead of asserting it after the 'as at other times' line.

weakest_line: It's one of the most asked questions about the Bible and most Christians can't answer it.
one_fix: Replace the 'you'll know what to say' close with a real prompt that invites a response. Split the run-on Genesis 5 / 'mother of all living' sentence so the evidence lands one piece at a time.
Lead with the buried text puzzle: why would God ask Adam 'Where art thou?' if He already knew? Drop the devotional 'we/you' opener and the assumptions about the viewer skipping church.

weakest_line: And if you're here to stand for God's word, welcome to the Valiant.
one_fix: Cut one of the three thinkers (Schellenberg, Kierkegaard, Pascal) and let the golden calf weeks after Sinai carry the proof. Drop the channel-identity sign-off, which assumes who the viewer is.

weakest_line: Some Christians also wonder about this question sometimes.
one_fix: Address the hard half of the hook ('forever') with specific text instead of stacking familiar verses. Stop using Revelation 3:20 (written to a church) and John 10:10 out of context, including the claim that this is 'how the Bible ends'.

weakest_line: So God gave us free will, and He tells us plainly which way to choose.
one_fix: Ground the answer in Genesis 2 instead of hypothetical steal and covet analogies. God said 'of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat' with only one exception, so the text itself shows that one tree was the space for choice.
